title: Signatures of Leptophilic Baryogenesis at Muon Colliders
abstract: The baryon asymmetry of the Universe may be produced in a model with 3 Higgs fields, a Higgs Troika, without the need for a strong first order electroweak phase transition. The couplings of the new Higgs fields to Standard Model fermions are assumed in accord with the "Spontaneous Flavor Violation (SFV)" framework, in order to avoid large deviations from flavor physics constraints. We consider a leptophilic version of SFV and outline its potential signatures at future muon colliders, envisioned to be multi-TeV partonic center of momentum machines. Hence, they provide optimal venues to search for the leptophilic Higgs Troika baryogenesis mechanism. The projected reach for signals of the new scalars allows for probing the key components of the baryogenesis model at scales that accommodate cosmological requirements.

title: 21 cm Cosmology of Boosted Dark Matter
abstract: The formation history of low-mass halos is sensitive to the properties of dark matter. At low redshift, nonlinear evolution and baryonic processes can obscure this information. The 21 cm signal provides access to a high-redshift stage of structure formation, when the abundance and clustering of low-mass halos retain direct sensitivity to the mass and interactions of dark matter. Boosted dark matter (BDM) realizes this possibility through a two-component scenario in which the annihilation of the heavier component converts part of the mass difference into kinetic energy of the lighter component. Self-interactions redistribute this energy and generate pressure support, suppressing small-scale density perturbations even for dark matter masses in the MeV range. We calculate the global 21 cm brightness temperature and its power spectrum in BDM cosmology. The reduced abundance of low-mass halos delays the global absorption feature and shifts the characteristic redshift evolution of the power spectrum. We assess the projected sensitivity of SKA1-Low to these signatures. The sensitivity is strongest at intermediate light-component fractions, where both components remain sufficiently abundant for self-heating to affect structure formation. For $\sigma_{\rm self1}/m_1\simeq0.1\,{\rm cm^2\,g^{-1}}$, models with $0.2\lesssim r_1\lesssim0.7$ can be distinguished from the fiducial $\Lambda$CDM prediction at the $95\%$ confidence level under the optimistic forecast. We compare our results with existing direct-detection bounds from SENSEI and prospects for BDM searches at large-volume neutrino experiments, including Super-/Hyper-Kamiokande, JUNO, and DUNE. This comparison highlights the unique and complementary role of high-redshift surveys in testing BDM models.

title: The SymTFT and Quantum Phases of Matter
abstract: The symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT) provides a unified framework for ordinary and generalized symmetries of quantum many-body systems. By encoding symmetry in a topological theory in one higher dimension, it separates symmetry data from the details of a specific quantum system. In this review, we give a pedagogical introduction to this framework and survey its applications to phases of quantum matter. For fusion category symmetries in ${(1+1)}$d, we explain how the SymTFT characterizes anomalies, classifies gapped phases, and organizes the symmetry structure of gapless phases. We also give a broad overview of further developments of this framework, including extensions to symmetries in higher dimensions, continuous symmetries, fermionic systems, mixed states, and spacetime symmetries.

title: Feebly-Interacting Particle Searches
abstract: In the last several years, feebly-interacting particles (FIPs) have moved from "exotica" to the mainstream of particle physics. This development is fueled by three motivations: FIPs are one of two broad possibilities for new particles, FIPs are as well motivated by dark matter as WIMPs, and FIPs are connected to important problems in particle physics. I review these motivations and then briefly highlight recent progress in a few areas, including axion-like particles, dark photons and other gauge bosons, the X17 anomaly, quirks, and the Forward Physics Facility.

title: Plugging the Pion Chimney
abstract: Heavy QCD axions and other gluon-coupled axion-like particles (ALPs) with masses from MeV to GeV are well motivated and have been searched for extensively. However, a window around the neutral pion mass, the so-called pion chimney, has escaped every search. There the ALP mixes strongly with the $\pi^0$ and therefore shares its experimental signatures. We show that the chimney can be closed with existing LHC data. The key point is that mixing changes the lifetimes of the two mass eigenstates but does not make them equal, and at LHC energies the states are boosted enough for the lifetime to decide whether they escape the detector or decay inside it. The ATLAS monojet search constrains the first case and the ATLAS inclusive photon measurement the second, and together they exclude the chimney up to the cutoff of the ALP effective theory. Above the cutoff, LHC searches for the colored states of the simplest ultraviolet completions exclude the rest. We also show that the bound from the $K^+$ width does not reach the chimney, because an ALP passes the same selection as a $\pi^0$, and we derive an independent, purely kinematic constraint from the measured $\pi^\pm$-$\pi^0$ mass splitting.

title: Supernova Bounds on Neutrino Dipole Moments from a Modern Perspective
abstract: Neutrinos may have nonstandard magnetic dipole moments $\mu_\nu$. In the dense cores of supernovae (SNe), these would convert part of the neutrinos into sterile, right-handed states through the electromagnetic fluctuations of the charged plasma. The streaming sterile neutrinos with 100-MeV energies can convert back to standard neutrinos in the Galactic magnetic field, leading to a high-energy neutrino flux unobserved from the historical SN 1987A. We reassess the production rates, including scattering on both protons and electrons, and, building upon advances in SN simulations and in the description of the Milky Way magnetic field, we revisit the bounds on magnetic dipole moments. We find for Dirac electron neutrinos $\mu_{\nu_e} \lesssim 4.8 \times 10^{-13} \mu_B$, superseding all existing terrestrial and astrophysical constraints.

title: Active Galactic Nuclei as Beyond the Standard Model Laboratories: a White Paper
abstract: Multi-messenger and multi-wavelength observations of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) can provide otherwise inaccessible knowledge about physics Beyond the Standard Model (BSM), and may even lead to its discovery. Realizing this potential hinges on two parallel efforts: advancing our understanding of AGN and of the dark matter around them, and identifying the BSM signatures that are at once promising and robust against the gaps in that understanding. These fields have attracted growing interest in recent years, also motivated by the IceCube association of neutrinos to individual AGN, yet we have only begun to explore their cross-fertilization. This white paper offers a new perspective on this interdisciplinary endeavor. It concisely reviews the state of the art in each field and at their interface, and identifies the key open questions that must be addressed to strengthen our prospects for learning about BSM physics with AGN.

title: Thermal Composite Dark Matter at LZ
abstract: We show that stable fermionic resonances of Composite Higgs models provide a thermal inelastic Dark Matter interpretation of the high-energy nuclear-recoil event LZ230616. Their stability follows from an exact accidental parity of the strong sector. Annihilation channels from composite interactions link the thermal relic mass to the strong coupling, allowing masses well beyond the pure electroweak prediction. We identify three scenarios in which the neutral states form a split pseudo-Dirac pair, distinguished by the origin of the inelastic coupling to the $Z$ boson. In the pure electroweak regime, the pair consists of the neutral components of a complex Higgsino-like doublet. Its unsuppressed inelastic $Z$ coupling requires Dark Matter masses above 20 TeV. In the pure strong regime, the suppressed $Z$ coupling of neutral states with vanishing hypercharge arises from strong interactions alone, allowing for smaller splittings and TeV-scale masses. In the third regime, which interpolates between the previous two, the neutral components of multiplets with different hypercharge are mixed. This enhances their inelastic coupling, accommodating the LZ event for masses of a few TeV and splittings around 300 keV, with mixing angles of order $10^\circ$. All three cases provide a thermal Dark Matter candidate able to explain the LZ event, consistently with the solar-capture bounds, the LZ high-energy sideband, and gamma-ray indirect searches.

title: Smuggling baryon asymmetry through strong washout
abstract: We propose a scheme in which a primordial net baryon number generated at or around the unification scale may survive subsequent strong washout phases associated with active sphalerons and interactions of right-handed neutrinos inherent to thermal leptogenesis. A simple realization of this, namely, a long-lived scalar population injecting the net $B-L$ it carries into the Standard Model matter sector late enough to be safe from a strong washout, is constructed and studied in the context of a simple Pati-Salam scalar sector with a heavy $SU(4)_C$ sextet scalar.

title: Perturbative QCD Analysis for the Electric Dipole Moment of $\Xi$ and $\Sigma$ Hyperons from CP-Violating Dipole Interactions
abstract: Hyperon electric dipole moments (EDMs) probe CP-violating interactions beyond the Standard Model. Motivated by the recent BESIII measurement [Ablikim et al., Science 393, 1027] and the perturbative QCD analysis of the $\Lambda$ EDM form factor $d_\Lambda$ [Chen et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 051902], we extend the perturbative QCD calculation of the EDM form factor to the $\Xi$ and $\Sigma$ hyperons. We derive factorization formulas from quark EDM and chromoelectric dipole moment contributions in terms of leading-twist light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs). Using lattice-QCD results for the LCDAs and the strange-quark dipole moment ranges inferred from the BESIII $d_\Lambda$ bound and neutron EDM constraints, we obtain the conditional estimates $-4.8 \times 10^{-18} < d_{\Xi^-} < 1.8\times10^{-18}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $-6.1\times10^{-19} < d_{\Sigma^+} < 2.4\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ at the scale of ${J/\psi}$ mass. Dedicated searches at BESIII and the future Super Tau-Charm Factory could further constrain these quark-level sources of CP violation.

title: Mapping the multimessenger horizon for $\gamma$-ray counterparts of cosmic neutrinos
abstract: The joint detection of high-energy neutrinos and $\gamma$-rays offers a powerful probe of the most energetic astrophysical accelerators, linking hadronic interactions to observable signatures across cosmic distances. Understanding the conditions under which these two messengers can be simultaneously observed is essential for identifying and characterizing the sources of cosmic neutrinos. In this work, we examine the detectability of $\gamma$-ray cascades associated with neutrino production in source environments that are gamma-ray transparent, focusing on how electromagnetic cascades evolve as $\gamma$-rays propagate through intergalactic space. By modeling photon interactions with the extragalactic background light and deflections in intergalactic magnetic fields, we determine the minimum neutrino fluence for transient emission and neutrino flux for steady emission required to produce a $\gamma$-ray counterpart detectable by $\gamma$-ray observatories, such as Fermi-LAT, HAWC, or LHAASO. This defines a ``multimessenger horizon" -- the region in flux-distance parameter space where neutrinos and $\gamma$-rays are jointly observable. We consider both energy-binned injection tied to IceCube's sensitivity and a continuous power-law spectrum extending from TeV to PeV energies. Our results reveal that detectability depends strongly on redshift, magnetic field strength, and photon energy, with higher-energy cascades suffering greater attenuation inside filamentary structures. The framework provides new constraints on source opacity, baryon loading, and neutrino production mechanisms, offering a predictive tool for interpreting current events and guiding future multimessenger campaigns.

title: Analytic next-to-leading order electroweak corrections to Higgs boson pair production in the forward limit
abstract: We calculate next-to-leading order electroweak corrections for Higgs boson pair production in the gluon fusion channel, in the forward limit. We perform an analytic calculation and obtain a final result for the partonic cross section that depends explicitly on all kinematic parameters and particle masses. We describe our method, which can be readily applied to similar processes. We observe rapid convergence within the validity range of the forward expansion. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the entire phase space can be covered when this approach is combined with the high-energy expansion.

title: A new angle on coherence-violating logarithms in color-singlet processes
abstract: We introduce a new formulation for the resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the transverse energy flow in rapidity gaps in the Drell-Yan process. Our formalism allows us to resum coherence-violating logarithms in the gap cross section in the phenomenologically important regime where the gap size is comparable to the logarithm of the transverse energy. In the formal small gap limit, our result reduces to the known state-of-the-art resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the Drell-Yan process. However, we identify sizable new corrections even for moderate gap widths that significantly modify the phenomenological picture for LHC applications. This work will form an important element of future extensions to a range of global and non-global observables.

title: $B\to K a$ decays in QCD factorization and revised bounds on ALP couplings
abstract: Rare flavor-changing processes such as $B\to K a$ offer sensitive probes of axion-like particles (ALPs) for masses below a few GeV. We study this process in the framework of QCD factorization and ALP effective theory, in which the ALP couples to the Standard Model (SM) fermions through shift-invariant derivative interactions. In contrast to previous studies, where flavor violation arises solely from flavor-changing ALP couplings, we also include the contributions proportional to flavor-conserving ALP couplings, in which the flavor change is mediated by the weak interactions of the SM. Based on this analysis, we derive upper bounds on both flavor-changing and flavor-conserving ALP couplings at low energies. Then we consider the UV scenario of a "minimally flavor-violating ALP", which features flavor-universal ALP-fermion couplings at very high energies, and evaluate the resulting constraints on the UV couplings.

title: On the Structure of the Nuclear-Clock Isotope $^{229}$Th Beyond Quadratic Order
abstract: Precision measurements of the exceptionally low-energy nuclear transition of $^{229}$Th, offer an extraordinary sensitivity to a variety of new light fields. However, interpreting such measurements requires nuclear-structure information beyond what is currently constrained by spectroscopy. We develop a systematic description of the electric multipole interactions governing the hyperfine structure of ${}^{229}$Th, including the hexadecapole contribution, and perform a symmetry-based analysis of the resulting hyperfine splittings in crystalline environments. Hyperfine spectroscopy generally constrains combinations of nuclear moments and crystal-field gradients, leading to degeneracies when higher multipole interactions are allowed. We then combine experimental nuclear observables, particle-rotor relations, and a deformed-Fermi charge-density model to investigate the electromagnetic contribution to the nuclear clock's sensitivity to variations in the fine-structure constant. We find that higher-order nuclear deformation and state-dependent differences in the radial charge distribution of the clock states can substantially alter the predicted sensitivity, introducing large uncertainties that are not constrained by existing measurements. Our results highlight the importance of combining nuclear and solid-state theory with complementary measurements, including spectroscopy of higher-spin states, to constrain the nuclear structure and improve predictions of the clock's sensitivity to new physics. Our symmetry-based analysis also provides a framework for using hyperfine spectroscopy to investigate local defect symmetries in crystalline hosts.

title: Probing scalar-mediated Lorentz violation with hydrogen masers and spin-precession of molecules
abstract: We propose using hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession experiments, traditionally employed in precision frequency measurements and searches for the electron electric dipole moment, as complementary probes of light scalar-mediated, spin-dependent fifth forces. We investigate their sensitivity to Lorentz-violating interactions mediated by scalars with masses ranging from $\mathcal{O}(10^{-4}~\mu\mathrm{eV})$ to $\mathcal{O}(10~\mathrm{keV})$. While hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession measurements probe different combinations of Lorentz-violating couplings, we find that the strongest projected sensitivities can be achieved using spin-precession of ultracold molecules, benefiting from their extended coherence times. These experimental approaches provide access to previously unexplored regions of parameter space, probing interaction ranges extending from centimeter to sub-angstrom scales. Our proposals highlight the potential of precision atomic and molecular experiments to search for new spin-dependent scalar-mediated interactions and violations of fundamental spacetime symmetries.

title: Probing $\tau$ lepton dipole moments at multi-TeV muon colliders
abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of future multi-TeV muon colliders to the electromagnetic and weak dipole moments of the $\tau$ lepton within the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory. We consider $\tau^+\tau^-$ production through $\mu^+\mu^-$ annihilation and vector-boson scattering, electroweak-boson-associated $\tau$ production, and the radiative Higgs decay $H\to\tau^+\tau^-\gamma$. At high energies, the dipole-induced contributions quadratic in the Wilson coefficients become particularly important, with associated Higgs production, $\mu^+\mu^-\to\tau^+\tau^-H$, providing the strongest sensitivity through energy-enhanced contact interactions. The remaining channels offer complementary probes of the underlying dipole operators. For a $10$~TeV muon collider with an integrated luminosity of $10\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, we obtain combined sensitivities at the nominal $95\%$ confidence level of $|\Delta a_\tau|<1.2\times10^{-5}$, $|d_\tau|<6.6\times10^{-20}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$, $|\Delta a_\tau^Z|<1.8\times10^{-5}$, and $|d_\tau^Z|<1.0\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$. Compared with FCC-ee projections, the muon collider offers substantially stronger sensitivity to the electric dipole moments, while both facilities offer complementary probes of magnetic dipole moments. These results motivate further studies incorporating realistic detector effects and systematic uncertainties.

title: A Forecast for Testing the Decreasing $H_0$ Trend in Time-Delay Cosmography
abstract: In 2019 the H0LiCOW/TDCOSMO collaboration reported a decreasing Hubble constant $H_0$ trend with lens redshift in the flat $\Lambda$CDM model at low statistical significance ($< 2 \sigma$). The signal is expected if physics is missing from the $\Lambda$CDM model in the late universe. In the wake of recent TDCOSMO 2026 results, we revisit the feature. Although the statistical significance of the trend has increased in a like-for-like comparison with earlier studies, propagating mass-sheet transformation (MST) uncertainties reduces the significance to $\sim 1 \sigma$. As a result, Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) currently favours a constant $H_0$ over a decreasing $H_0$ in the ratio 2.4:1. Nevertheless, we highlight good agreement on a negative slope with independent observables and forecast that approximately 40 and 90 lenses will be required to substantiate the trend at $\sim 2 \sigma$ and $\sim 3 \sigma$ significance, respectively, if the feature is physical and current uncertainties are representative. Even now, it is evident that the TDCOSMO 2026 $H_0$ constraint $H_0 \approx 71$ km/s/Mpc reflects an average over the lens redshift distribution and is naturally anchored at intermediate lens redshifts.

title: Fundamental physics with quantum sensors in space
abstract: Quantum sensors such as atomic clocks, atom interferometers, and atomic magnetometers can be used as sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model. Space offers microgravity, long baselines, low environmental noise, access to varying gravitational potentials, and unique opportunities involving the Sun, Moon, planets, and asteroids. These proceedings of the Aspen Center for Physics workshop on "Fundamental physics in space with quantum sensors," held February 22-27, 2026, summarize the scientific case, current capabilities, and space mission concepts for investigating dark matter, testing general relativity, and detecting gravitational waves in frequency bands inaccessible from the ground.

title: Double parton scattering singularities in two-loop gluon-fusion amplitudes
abstract: Gluon fusion to two massive colour singlets can develop a double parton scattering (DPS) singularity as $p_T\to0$: each gluon splits, and its daughters fuse pairwise. We determine two-loop logarithms using a common kernel and derive finite matching functions analytically for gluon and quark splittings. Normalised to one loop, the cubic coefficient changes sign between channels. Complete $gg\to HH$, $gg\to AA$ and $gg\to ZZ$ amplitudes confirm the predicted colour, helicity and parity dependence and phase. The kernel gives leading DPS logarithms for other pairs with this DPS configuration.

title: Search for the low-mass isotropic signature of QCD instantons in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV using the ATLAS detector
abstract: This Letter presents the first search for QCD instanton-induced events at the LHC. Instantons are semi-classical solutions of the Yang-Mills equations of QCD and correspond to non-perturbative tunneling between topologically distinct vacuum sectors. The search is performed in 1.6 $\text{nb}^{-1}$ of very low instantaneous luminosity proton-proton collision data collected by the ATLAS detector at 13 TeV. Angular variables based on reconstructed charged-particle tracks are used to discriminate the expected rest-frame isotropy of low-mass instanton events from the minimum-bias background. The minimum-bias event background is predicted using a data-driven technique and reweighted Monte Carlo models. A profile-likelihood fit is performed in a two-dimensional classifier variable to extract a possible signal contribution, yielding an excess of low-mass isotropic events with an observed significance of $3.5\sigma$.

title: Flavor Entanglement as a CPT Violation Witness in Neutrino Oscillations
Gravitational waves from cosmological first-order phase transitions with fluctuation-induced friction
abstract: We study gravitational-wave production in a cosmological first-order phase transition with fluctuation-induced friction using three-dimensional lattice simulations of two coupled scalar fields. Kinetic and gradient energy in the additional field $s$ accumulates near the expanding bubble walls of $\phi$ and affects their motion. The contribution from $s$ exceeds that from $\phi$ at the spectral peak and has a slope similar to that of the bulk flow model over a finite interval above the peak. In the high-wave-number (UV) direction, $\phi$ dominates and the total spectrum develops a broad feature. For the larger coupling, slowly contracting false vacuum remnants persist long after bubble merger.

title: Top-Quark Physics after Evidence for Toponium
abstract: The top quark decays before it hadronizes, and toponium, the t\bar t bound state, was long thought unobservable as a resonance. CMS and ATLAS each report an excess of top-quark pairs at threshold, above five standard deviations over fixed-order quantum chromodynamics (QCD), and CMS confirms it in a second decay channel. Its angular distributions match the color-singlet pseudoscalar quasi-bound state \eta_t of nonrelativistic QCD, although an additional pseudoscalar boson is not excluded and higher-order fixed-order QCD accounts for part of the enhancement. We review the theory, ATLAS's nominal Green's-function signal model, and the measurements, whose cross sections range from about 3 to 13 pb. Part of the spread comes from the signal model and part persists between analyses using the same model. We discuss consequences for entanglement, the top mass, and heavy-pseudoscalar searches. We then review the top-quark program, from mass definitions to electroweak precision, flavor, the charge-conjugation and parity (CP) structure of the top Yukawa coupling, supersymmetry, multi-top production, and effective field theory. We close with prospects at the High-Luminosity LHC and future colliders, where an e^+e^- threshold scan can determine the top-quark mass in a short-distance scheme to a few tens of MeV.

title: Triangle singularity with different dynamical couplings
abstract: We carry out a systematic study of the impact of dynamical couplings of the vertices on the manifestations of the triangle singularity (TS) in the loop amplitude. Twelve combinations of external and internal spin-parity quantum numbers, covering the $PPS$, $VPP$, $VVP$, $VPA$, $VVV$, $VVA$, and $VVS$ effective vertices, are enumerated. Each loop amplitude is reduced via the Passarino--Veltman decomposition into scalar integrals $A_{0}$, $B_{0}$, and $C_{0}$, whose Lorentz-scalar coefficients encode the dynamical content of the vertices. Using the masses and kinematics of the $\eta(1405)\to\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0}$ transition via the $K^{*}\bar{K}K$ loop with the intermediate $f_{0}(980)$ resonance in the $\pi^+\pi^-$ invariant spectrum as a common numerical benchmark for the twelve spin-parity assignments, we find that the same loop topology produces three distinct phenomena which manifest through the lineshapes, i.e. a narrow peak dominated by the $C_{0}$ contribution; a suppressed peak in which the $B_{0}$ and $C_{0}$ function contributions are comparable; and a cusp-like profile in which the coefficient of the leading Landau logarithm vanishes at the physical TS point. These results indicate that the visibility of a TS enhancement is not fixed by the Landau condition alone but reshaped by the detailed dynamics involved in the loop transitions.

title: Lie-Poisson Formulation of Dissipative Spin Hydrodynamics
abstract: Covariance and the second law cannot fix how fluid flow couples to spin, since reversible couplings produce no entropy. We show that the spin commutation relations and the Poincar\'e algebra fix these couplings. Reversibly, a flow exerts no torque on the spin: its magnitude per particle is conserved, its direction is Fermi--Walker transported, and spin--shear couplings reflect a deforming triad. The magnitude changes only through higher multipoles, as in spinor condensates, or dissipation, whose first-order spin--shear coupling reorients the spin away from the vorticity above a critical shear rate.

title: An exact separability criterion for the $J/\psi\Lambda$ spin state in $\Lambda_b^0\to J/\psi\,\Lambda$ decays at the LHC
abstract: We derive an exact separability criterion for the spin state of the $J/\psi\Lambda$ pair produced in $\Lambda_b^0\to J/\psi(\to\mu^+\mu^-)\,\Lambda(\to p\pi^-)$ decays, taking into account the $\Lambda_b^0$ polarization at the LHC. Within the four-amplitude family $\{a_\pm,b_\pm\}$, the system is separable if and only if $(1+P_b\cos\theta)a_+b_+=(1-P_b\cos\theta)a_-b_-=P_b\sin\theta b_+b_-=0$, where $\theta$ is the $\Lambda$ production angle defined in the LHC environment. We propose a profiled likelihood ratio test to probe entanglement in the full five-dimensional angular analysis. Idealized pseudoexperiments compare this test with a negativity test and a test based on the angular moments $M_7$ and $M_9$ for rejecting the $a_+=b_-=0$ hypothesis. At both $3\sigma$ and $5\sigma$ significance, the proposed test achieves a $90\%$ rejection power with about half as many signal events as the other two methods. These results support the prospects for entanglement evidence with samples on the existing scale and for observation with larger samples.

title: Effects of QCD Equation of State on Cosmological Parameters and Stochastic Gravitational-Waves Spectrum
abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic evolution of the early Universe across the QCD crossover and up to the electroweak (EW) scale, emphasizing the systematic impact of the QCD equation of state (EoS) and electroweak degrees of freedom on thermodynamic variables, cosmological parameters, and gravitational-wave observables. Using the HotQCD EoS as a baseline, we employ Gaussian Process (GP) regression to generate ensembles of 1000 thermodynamically consistent EoS samples, each extrapolated to high temperatures with and without EW contributions. For each ensemble, we solve the Friedmann equations to obtain the expansion history and compute gravitational-wave (GW) observables, including the instantaneous spectral tilt $n_{gw}(f)$ and the normalized GW energy density $\Omega_{gw}(f)/\Omega_{gw}^{\rm rad}$. We find that including the EW sector is the dominant effect across all observables, outweighing differences among QCD baseline models that share the same lattice calibration. In particular, EW contributions drive the EoS toward the radiation-dominated limit earlier, reduce excursions of the speed of sound toward the causality bound, suppress transient fluctuations in the Hubble and kinematic parameters near $t \sim 10^{-5}$ s, and qualitatively change the GW spectrum from a strongly frequency-dependent signal to a flat, suppressed plateau. These results demonstrate that accurate modeling of the electroweak sector is essential for an unbiased extraction of QCD-era physics from the stochastic gravitational-wave background.

title: AI-Assisted Analysis of CMS Open Data: Prompt J/psi Cross-Section Measurements in pp and Peripheral PbPb Collisions at sqrt(S)= 7 TeV and sqrt(sNN) = 2.76 TeV
abstract: We investigate the use of an artificial-intelligence (AI) coding agent, supervised by human physicists, for collider physics analyses using CMS Open Data. OpenAI Codex performs dimuon event selection, two-dimensional invariant-mass and decay-length fits, Monte Carlo detector simulations, and systematic uncertainty evaluation after acquiring physics and experimental knowledge from published studies and external references, with human review at each stage. The workflow is tested on two CMS datasets, with custom full-detector simulations used to determine acceptance and reconstruction efficiencies. In proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 7 TeV, prompt J/psi differential cross sections are measured versus transverse momentum and rapidity. The ratios of remeasured to published CMS cross sections have a mean of 1.000 and an RMS spread of 0.215 across 39 bins. In peripheral (50-100% centrality) PbPb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 2.76 TeV, the corresponding prompt J/psi fiducial cross-section ratios have a mean of 1.158 and an RMS spread of 0.225 across six intervals. We identify agent failure modes and demonstrate the importance of structured human review in ensuring reliable results.

title: Quantum phase transition and superselection sectors in two-color one-flavor matrix QCD at weak coupling
abstract: We numerically investigate the weak-coupling (small $g$) regime of the matrix model of $SU(2)$ gauge theory coupled to one flavor of massless fundamental quarks. The theory possesses a global Pauli-G\"ursey $SU(2)_B$ symmetry, which organizes physical states of spin $J$ into sectors labelled by its representation $B$. We find localization-delocalization quantum phase transitions (QPTs) in multiple $(B,J)$ sectors at sector-dependent critical couplings $g_\ast^{BJ}$. Direct evaluation of the localization probability reveals that the ground states are predominantly localized near $A_i=0$ for $g<g_\ast^{BJ}$, but become almost entirely expelled from this region for $g>g_*^{BJ}$. The QPTs in different sectors exhibit distinct features, and we establish that quark-glue interactions are essential for these transitions. The transitions are singular: the ground state expectation value of $\text{Tr}(A_iA_i)$ remains finite for $g< g_\ast^{BJ}$, whereas it diverges as $g$ approaches $g_\ast^{BJ}$ from above. We show that the two limiting ground states on either side of $g_\ast^{BJ}$ belong to distinct superselection sectors. Furthermore, as $g$ approaches $g_\ast^{BJ}$ from above, the ground state localizes on a submanifold (of codimension 2) of the gauge configuration space, with the spin and color of its glue components becoming locked.

title: How can every physicist become a Bohmian
abstract: The Bohmian interpretation of quantum mechanics is controversial because it attributes deterministic trajectories to microscopic particles. We propose a reformulation that sidesteps this controversy: rather than applying Bohmian mechanics at the microscopic level, we recast it as an effective deterministic description of the macroscopic pointer of a measuring apparatus, with no claims about the fundamental nature of the microscopic world. In this form, the Bohmian trajectory becomes a practical tool for visualizing the emergence of a definite measurement outcome, broadly acceptable to physicists who would otherwise reject the Bohmian program.

title: Millicharged Fermions as Dark Matter: Theoretical Modeling and Experimental Detection
abstract: Fermions with a small effective charge, $\qeff\ll1$, arise from kinetic mixing between an unbroken (or nearly unbroken) dark $U(1)'$ and electromagnetism, or from a genuinely fractional charge. Millicharged particles (mCPs) inherit the Pauli-exclusion constraints on fermionic dark matter (DM) in galaxies, while adding a long-range plasma phenomenology absent for neutral candidates. This review connects three strands: (i) the symmetry structure, cosmology and astrophysical bounds of millicharged fermions, comparing kinetic-mixing and fractional-charge realizations; (ii) the role of mCPs in galactic halo formation and dynamics, and when they fit the Ruffini--Arg\"uelles--Rueda (RAR) self-gravitating core--halo model; and (iii) experimental techniques for detecting mCPs trapped on Earth, arriving from the galactic halo, or emitted by the Sun. We show that a collisionless halo of keV--MeV millicharged fermions requires $\alpha'\lesssim7\times10^{-13}$--$2\times10^{-10}$, depending on mass and velocity, orders of magnitude below the coupling needed for thermal freeze-out via $\chi\bar\chi\to A'A'$ in the Milky Way and dwarf galaxies. A RAR halo made of the mCP itself thus needs non-thermal production, a charge-symmetric plasma and very small dark coupling, whereas a sub-dominant mCP component can be added without changing the halo. We close with open theoretical and experimental challenges and a summary of the allowed mCP parameter space.

title: Scalar inelastic scattering of pseudo-Majorana dark matter through a radion portal
abstract: We investigate a radion portal for pseudo-Majorana dark matter as an interpretation of the high-recoil event LZ230616. In contrast to the familiar pseudo-Dirac regime, the pseudo-Majorana structure allows a dominant scalar transition while suppressing elastic scattering. Endothermic kinematics remove low-energy recoils, while the nuclear response shapes the surviving high-recoil spectrum. Combining the accepted LZ event count with the Born-level thermal relic abundance yields a reference solution with $m_\chi=1$ TeV, $\delta=340$ keV, and $m_r=30$ GeV. This solution lies within the published LZ spin-independent $\mathcal{O}_1^s$ interval and remains compatible with existing OPAL and CMS constraints, while a simplified HL-LHC diphoton projection could probe it. Solar neutrino searches offer a complementary test. The benchmark's energetic-daughter proxy rates are comparable in magnitude to the rate scales reconstructed from IceCube's direct $b\bar{b}$ and $\tau^+\tau^-$ templates. An illustrative IceCube-Gen2 rescaling suggests future sensitivity, while a model-specific assessment requires the radion-cascade neutrino spectra and detector response.

title: Impact of errors-on-errors on the PDF determination from combined HERA data
abstract: We study how the determination of parton distribution functions (PDFs) from the combined HERA inclusive deep-inelastic-scattering data is affected when the quoted sizes of the systematic errors are themselves treated as uncertain. We refer to these uncertainties informally as errors-on-errors and account for them using the Gamma Variance Model, which treats the squared quoted systematic errors as Gamma-distributed estimates of unknown variances. As a result, the usual quadratic nuisance parameter constraints in the $\chi^2$ are replaced with logarithmic ones. We present two applications of the framework. In the first, a robustness test estimates the largest errors-on-errors effects that could be present in our reproduction of the HERAPDF2.0 NNLO fit, reducing $\chi^2/n_{\rm dof}$ from 1363/1131 to 1306/1131, with the main impact concentrated at low Bjorken $x$ and low squared momentum transfer, $Q^2$. Comparable reductions are observed with a more flexible small-$x$ parametrisation, both at fixed NNLO and with NNLO+NLL$_x$ resummation. In the second, the error-on-error parameters are instead assigned a priori, as they would be in a PDF determination intended for publication. Taken together, the results indicate that errors-on-errors can account for a substantial part of the apparent data-theory tension in the combined HERA dataset, improving the inferred compatibility and widening the fitted PDF uncertainties without appreciably displacing the PDFs or cross-section predictions themselves.

title: Universal Mass Equation for Equal-Quantum Excited-States Sets~III
abstract: Using our simple logarithmic Universal Mass Equation, we considered heavy non-$q\bar{q}$ meson states. PDG2026 reported a series of mesons with quantum numbers not allowed for standard $q\bar{q}$ states. Using LQCD predictions, we evaluated a scalar $0^{++}$ and tensor $2^{++}$ glueball series for which predictions are available. This approach allows us to predict heavy states that require future experimental studies. Additionally, we consider the possible misidentification of some meson states.

title: Muon Collider: Towards the Energy Frontier
abstract: A muon collider has emerged as a compelling candidate for the next energy-frontier particle accelerator, combining the discovery potential of multi-TeV lepton collisions with a footprint and power consumption far smaller than existing or proposed hadron and electron-positron colliders. Advances over the past two decades in high-power targets, muon production and capture, ionization cooling, rapid acceleration, high-field magnets, collider ring design, and machine-detector integration have transformed the concept from a long-term vision into a credible path toward a future flagship facility. This review summarizes the physics opportunities, the accelerator complex's design and status, the unique experimental environment, recent technical achievements, ongoing international R&D, and remaining steps toward realizing a high-energy muon collider by the middle of the century.

title: Absolute luminosity calibration of the LHCb detector in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV with beam-gas imaging
authors: U. De Freitas Carneiro Da Graca
abstract: An absolute calibration of the luminosity for proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV with the LHCb detector in Run 2 of the LHC is presented. The calibration cross-section of the Vertex counter, a statistic based on reconstructed primary vertices, is measured using the beam-gas imaging method to be $\sigma_\mathrm{Vertex} = 57.61 \pm 0.06\ (stat) \pm 0.52\ (syst)$ mb, corresponding to a relative precision of 0.91%. This result provides around a factor of two improvement in the precision of the LHCb luminosity calibration used in previous cross-section measurements with this dataset. The largest systematic uncertainties arise from the imperfect knowledge of the beam-gas vertex resolution, the observed fill-by-fill spread of the cross-section, and the choice of transverse beam-profile fit model.

title: A Universal Axion in a Twin-QCD Sector
abstract: Dark matter may consist of multiple components with distinct particle-physics origins. We investigate a scenario in which a universal axion couples to both visible and twin QCD, with twin baryons providing a possible dominant dark-matter component. The presence of a second strongly interacting sector can substantially enhance the axion mass while preserving its role in resolving the strong-CP problem, provided the physical vacuum angles are appropriately aligned. For a representative uniformly rescaled twin spectrum with a confinement scale five times that of ordinary QCD, the axion mass is enhanced by approximately a factor of 25. Using lattice-informed QCD results and a two-temperature description of the early universe, we investigate the cosmological evolution and relative abundances of the dark-sector components. In a representative conditional numerical benchmark, axions account for a small percentage of the observed dark matter, while twin baryons could constitute the remainder for a suitable primordial baryon asymmetry. We also examine the implications for additional relativistic species, strong-CP alignment, and the interactions of stable twin matter. Our results provide a quantitative framework for exploring mixed axion--twin-baryon dark matter and identify the particle-physics and cosmological conditions necessary for a viable realization, including constraints from the thermal history and formation of cosmic structure.

title: Loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ at NLO+PS for LHC simulations: exact, fast scale and PDF event weights, theory uncertainties, and the limits of rescaled LO+PS
abstract: We study loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ production with charged-lepton and neutrino $Z$ decays at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD matched to parton showers, using public software at $\sqrt{s}=13$ and 13.6 TeV. An exact loop-amplitude cache reduces event-generation time by a factor of 26 with 450 scale and PDF weights, while Born suppression improves boosted-event statistics without changing the weighted prediction. We present inclusive results for both channels and charged-lepton differential and STXS Stage 1.3 predictions with theory uncertainties. At 13.6 TeV, fixed-order top-quark mass-scheme variations transferred to NLO+PS dominate the statistically precise central-Higgs STXS bins for $p_\mathrm{T}^V\ge150$ GeV, reaching 32-50%. An inclusive $K$ factor does not reproduce the boosted and jet-dependent NLO+PS spectra of the tested LO+PS samples, and the differences depend strongly on the shower prescription. For specified CMS- and ATLAS-style vetoed sources at 13.6 TeV, we construct separate charged-lepton and neutrino corrections using ensembles of gradient-boosted classifiers, with calibration, target-theory variations and transfer uncertainties. Independent tests show substantial improvement over inclusive rescaling in most tested distributions, but not uniform closure. In charged-lepton calibration comparisons, the median STXS uncertainty from transported NLO scales and transfer terms is 17% for both the CMS- and ATLAS-style corrections, compared with LO scale uncertainties of 28% and 26% at fixed $K$. These comparisons do not include the complete target-theory budget. The corrections do not restore the depleted hard-recoil population; the highest ATLAS-style $p_\mathrm{T}^H$ bin stays below NLO+PS even at the upper edge of its band. The setup, reference results, and source- and channel-specific models support new NLO+PS generation and reuse of existing samples within stated limits.

title: Imprints of Non-local Top-Higgs Interaction on Loop Induced Higgs Processes
abstract: A composite Higgs arising from an underlying strong sector generally has non-local interactions with the elementary sector, formulated in terms of momentum-dependent form factors. We construct the minimal Ball-Chiu-type vertices consistent with gauge-invariant non-local $\bar{t}th$ couplings containing Wilson lines, where recursive Ward-Takahashi identities connect the Yukawa interaction to higher-order contact interactions. For a symmetric monopole form factor motivated by lowest-resonance dominance, we compute the top-loop contributions to $gg \to h$ and $h \to \gamma\gamma$ amplitudes in closed form, and demonstrate a logarithmically enhanced deviation from the Standard Model. Current measurements at the LHC exclude the characteristic new physics scale below 3.6 TeV at $2\sigma$, while future colliders could extend the sensitivity to approximately 8 TeV.

title: Precision Muon Physics
abstract: The muon has become a versatile tool for fundamental physics. Measurements of muon decay determine the Fermi constant and establish the chiral structure of weak interactions. Measurements with stored muons and bound muons enable precision determinations of the muon charge, mass, and magnetic moment. These studies also provide far-reaching tests of bound-state QED and the Standard Model, as well as unique sensitivity to physics beyond our current understanding of the particles, forces, and laws of nature. We survey the landscape of precision muon physics, emphasizing both the physics reach and the experimental breadth. We highlight the range of techniques, from charged-particle timing, tracking, and polarimetry to storage-ring experiments, microwave resonance methods, and Doppler-free laser spectroscopy. We also describe the interplay between experimental work and theoretical developments in quantum electrodynamics, quantum chromodynamics, and effective field theory.

title: Flavor-dependent quark-mass scaling and the fate of the strange-matter window in self-bound quark stars
abstract: In the flavor-dependent QMDD model, self-bound $ud$ quark matter can be the ground state at vanishing pressure and convert into $uds$ matter through a first-order transition. So far the mass functional has used parameters $(a,C)$ common to all flavors; here we let the strange sector have its own coupling, $C_s=\alpha\,C_{u,d}$, and map the response of the zero-pressure parameter space. The $e^0_{ud}=930\,$MeV boundary is independent of $\alpha$ by construction, whereas increasing $\alpha$ enlarges the self-bound $ud$ domain and pushes the $e^0_{ud}=e^0_{uds}$ line towards larger $a$. The causality boundary $c^0_s=c$ is almost frozen near $a\simeq5.5$. The competition closes the strange-matter window at \RA{$\alpha_{\rm crit}\simeq1.136$}: above it every causal self-bound parametrization is $ud$ at zero pressure, so a first-order $ud\!\to\!uds$ transition must occur at higher pressure, though not necessarily inside a star, since the maximum mass may be reached below the transition density. The transition pressure and the energy-density jump grow monotonically with $\alpha$, both scale \RB{approximately} with the available-volume fraction $q=1-\kappa$, and the Seidov onset-instability diagnostic stays below unity.

title: Probing Lorentz-violating electrodynamics with CMB polarization. II. Updated constraints and forecasts for the Simons Observatory and LiteBIRD
abstract: We update the constraints on Lorentz-violating electrodynamics from the polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Within the minimal Standard Model Extension, we consider the renormalizable CPT-odd and CPT-even operators of the photon sector, which source cosmic birefringence and circular polarization, respectively. Combining Planck, Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) and South Pole Telescope (SPT) temperature and $E$-mode data with $B$-mode measurements from BICEP/Keck, SPT-3G D1 and SPTpol, we constrain the CPT-odd coefficients to $|k^{(3)}_{(V)00}|<7.75\times10^{-45}$ GeV and $|\mathbf{k_{AF}}|<3.82\times10^{-45}$ GeV at 95% credible level. These are the strongest bounds to date from any probe, and are driven by the SPT-3G D1 $B$-mode data. For the first time in this type of analysis, we also include the Planck PR4 $EB$ spectrum, which yields a mild preference for a non-zero $|k^{(3)}_{(V)00}|$. For the CPT-even coefficient, we find $k_{F,E+B}<5.99\times10^{-32}$. Including the latest circular polarization measurements from the Cosmology Large Angular Scale Surveyor (CLASS) tightens this bound by about 7%. This is the first time that CMB circular polarization data contribute to constraining this coefficient. Finally, we forecast the sensitivity of the Simons Observatory (SO) and LiteBIRD. With linear polarization only, the two experiments are complementary, with SO tightening the CPT-even bound by about 30% and LiteBIRD the CPT-odd ones by 40 to 45%. Exploiting the sensitivity to circular polarization provided by the non-idealities of its half-wave plate, LiteBIRD could also improve the CPT-even bound by more than an order of magnitude.

title: Analytic Two-Loop Classical Bremsstrahlung Amplitude in Electrodynamics
abstract: We compute the leading long-wavelength term of the two-loop five-point amplitude for photon emission in the scattering of two massive spinless charges. Classical consistency suggests that two Coulomb exchanges dress the radiative tree amplitude. We show that this iteration accounts for the entire leading term and evaluate the resulting convolution. At fixed external transfer, the exchanges shift the momentum in the tree numerator, thereby changing the relative weights of its two polarization structures. We determine both coefficients at nonzero photon frequency and general relative velocity, with exact dependence on the spacetime dimension.

title: Electromagnetic form factors of the hidden-charm pentaquarks in a coupled-channel unitary approach
abstract: We study the electromagnetic form factors of the hidden-charm pentaquarks $P_c(4312)$, $P_c(4440)$ and $P_c(4457)$ and of their four heavy-quark spin partners, treated as $\bar D^{(*)}\Sigma_c^{(*)}$ hadronic molecules. The states are poles of a coupled-channel unitary amplitude with a vector-meson exchange kernel that respects heavy-quark spin symmetry. The form factors are the residues at the double pole of the photon-coupled amplitude. The current consists of one-body currents and a photon--four-hadron vertex, which we construct for this channel space. Its gauged-kernel part ensures the charge normalization through the compositeness sum rule, while its contact parts contain couplings that the model does not determine. For $J^P=\tfrac12^-$, $\tfrac12^-$, $\tfrac32^-$ and pointlike constituents, the mean squared distances between the constituents of the three observed states are $0.85-0.47i$, $0.35-0.18i$ and $1.76-0.57i\,\mathrm{fm}^2$. Within $2\%$, they equal the zero-range value $1/(4\mu_{\rm red} B_c)$, with reduced mass $\mu_{\rm red}$ and complex binding energy $B_c$, times the effective-range factor of the amplitude. The real parts of the magnetic moments are $1.7$, $-0.9$ and $1.3\,\mu_N$, within $11\%$ of the additive moments of the constituents. Variations of the constituent moments and of the magnetic contact couplings within bounds from dimensional analysis give the ranges $0.8$ to $2.0$, $-1.3$ to $-0.2$ and $0.2$ to $1.8\,\mu_N$. The charge radii depend also on the constituent structure and on electric contact currents. The photon loops of open channels have a triangle singularity at spacelike momentum transfer. We specify the analytic continuation of the residue in $Q^2$ and give the difference between its two adjacent branches in closed form.

title: Bayesian Multimessenger Constraints on Self-Bound Quark Stars in Revised Perturbative QCD
abstract: We perform a Bayesian multimessenger analysis of self-bound two-flavor $ud$ quark matter described by a thermodynamically consistent revised perturbative-QCD equation of state (EOS), incorporating the GW170817 tidal information, mass--radius measurements, and pulsar mass constraints. The resulting posterior medians and $68\%$ credible intervals are $B_0^{1/4}=137.66^{+1.72}_{-1.86}\,\mathrm{MeV}$, $M_{\max}=2.166^{+0.035}_{-0.036}\,M_\odot$, $R_{1.4}=11.778^{+0.203}_{-0.196}\,\mathrm{km}$, and $\Lambda_{1.4}=768^{+90}_{-81}$. The posterior-predictive support probability for interpreting the $2.59\,M_\odot$ GW190814 secondary as a self-bound $ud$ quark star is of order $10^{-5}$, strongly disfavoring this interpretation within the adopted EOS framework. The reconstructed EOS exhibits characteristic self-bound behavior, with finite energy and baryon number densities at the zero-pressure surface and a median surface energy density of $\epsilon_{\rm surf}\simeq187\,\mathrm{MeV\,fm^{-3}}$. Its pressure is suppressed relative to both the noninteracting $ud+e$ gas and the representative MIT bag-model prediction. Although the running strong coupling decreases with increasing quark chemical potential, its central value in maximum-mass configurations correlates positively with $M_{\max}$, indicating stronger coupling and reduced perturbative reliability toward the high-mass end. Notably, the squared speed of sound remains nearly constant, varying from $c_s^2\simeq0.321$ to $0.324$ between canonical and maximum-mass configurations, whereas the conformal measure $\Delta=1/3-P/\epsilon$ decreases substantially from approximately $0.208$ to $0.076$. This demonstrates that an approximately constant sound speed does not necessarily imply approximate conformality. The relativistic adiabatic index also increases sharply near the zero-pressure surface, reflecting the self-bound nature of the EOS.

title: Complete Cosmological Collider Signatures from Right-handed Neutrino Loops
abstract: We study the complete cosmological collider (CC) signatures from right-handed neutrino loops with chemical-potential enhancement. These CC signals are induced by the inflaton-right-handed-neutrino interaction and can be extracted in the collinear squeezed configuration, which allows the right-handed-neutrino triangle loop to be factorized into the hard and soft parts. We precisely compute the soft part of the fermion loop for the first time by using the complete mode functions and the full loop integral, and treat the hard part as a tree-level subdiagram. We subtract the large-momentum asymptotic terms of the soft loop integrand and retain their finite contributions to the oscillation. We then evaluate the full spinor-helicity and Schwinger-Keldysh sums to obtain a finite, closed analytic formula for the complex clock coefficient. We further derive a compact formula for the leading CC signals in the large-chemical-potential expansion. We analyze the structure of the soft-part contribution by examining the sum of residues of the Mellin poles of the fermion propagators. For this, we demonstrate that the first local pole on each soft line contributes half of the asymptotic coefficient on one Schwinger-Keldysh path and the remaining local poles on the second soft line supply the other half.
